en: 1. Root Pairs (Mūlayamaka) 1.1.
Summary (Uddesa) 1.1.1.
Summary of the Section on Roots (Mūlavāra-uddesa)
1.1.1.1. The Fourfold Guide on the Wholesome Section (Kusalapada Nayacatukka) 1.1.1.1.1.
The Guide on the Roots (Mūlanaya) Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One.
Whatever states are wholesome, are they all rooted in the wholesome roots?
Or conversely, are all those things which are roots of the wholesome themselves wholesome states?
Whatever states are wholesome, are they all rooted in the same root as the wholesome roots?
Or again, are all those phenomena which share the same root as the wholesome roots themselves wholesome?
Are all those phenomena which share the same root as the wholesome roots mutually rooted in one another by virtue of that wholesome root?
Or again, are all those phenomena which are mutually rooted in one another by virtue of the wholesome roots themselves wholesome?
1.1.1.1.2. The Method of the Root of Roots (Mūlamūlanaya):
Are all those states that are wholesome rooted in a wholesome root?
Or conversely, are all those states that are rooted in a wholesome root themselves wholesome?
Whatever states are wholesome, are they all rooted in the same root as the wholesome roots?
Or conversely, whatever states are rooted in the same root as the wholesome roots, are they all wholesome states?
Whatever states are rooted in the same root as the wholesome roots, are they all mutually rooted in one another by way of the wholesome roots?
Or again, those which have mutual roots by way of a wholesome root—are all those states wholesome?
1.1.1.1.3. The Method of Roots:
Whatever states are wholesome, are they all rooted in the wholesome?
Or again, are all those things which have wholesome roots themselves wholesome?
Are all those things which are wholesome rooted in the same root as the wholesome roots?
Or again, are all those things which are rooted in the same root as the wholesome roots themselves wholesome?
Whatever phenomena have a single root by virtue of a wholesome root, are they all mutually rooted by that same wholesome root?
Or conversely, whatever phenomena are mutually rooted by a wholesome root, are all those phenomena wholesome?
1.1.1.1.4. The Method of Root-and-Rootedness.
Whatever states are wholesome, are they all rooted in a wholesome root?
Or conversely, whatever states are rooted in a wholesome root, are they all wholesome?
Whatever states are wholesome, are they all rooted in the same single wholesome root?
Or again, are all those phenomena which share the same root as the wholesome roots themselves wholesome?
Are all those phenomena which share the same root as the wholesome roots mutually rooted in one another with respect to the wholesome roots?
Or again, are all those phenomena which are mutually rooted in one another with respect to the wholesome roots themselves wholesome?
1.1.1.2. The Fourfold Guide on Unwholesome States (Akusalapada Nayacatukka) 1.1.1.2.1.
The Guide on Roots (Mūlanaya) Are all those states which are unwholesome (akusala) rooted in the unwholesome (akusalamūla)?
Or again, are all those things which are unwholesome roots unwholesome states?
Are all those things which are unwholesome states rooted in the same root as the unwholesome roots?
Or again, are all those things which are rooted in the same root as the unwholesome roots unwholesome states?
Whatever phenomena have an unwholesome root as their single root, do they all have one another as mutual roots because of that unwholesome root?
Or, conversely, whatever phenomena have one another as mutual roots because of an unwholesome root, are all those phenomena unwholesome?
1.1.1.2.2. The Method of Root and Sub-root.
Whatever states are unwholesome, are they all rooted in the unwholesome roots?
Or conversely, whatever states are rooted in the unwholesome roots, are they all unwholesome states?
Whatever states are unwholesome, are they all rooted in the same root as the unwholesome roots?
Furthermore, are all those phenomena which share the same root as the unwholesome roots themselves unwholesome?
Are all those phenomena that share the same root as the unwholesome roots mutually rooted in one another by way of the unwholesome roots?
And furthermore, are all those phenomena that are mutually rooted in one another by way of the unwholesome roots themselves unwholesome?
1.1.1.2.3. The Root Method (Mūlakanaya):
Are all those states which are unwholesome necessarily rooted in the unwholesome roots?
Or conversely, are all those states which are rooted in the unwholesome roots necessarily unwholesome states?
Whatever states are unwholesome, are they all rooted in the same root as the unwholesome roots?
Or conversely, whatever states are rooted in the same root as the unwholesome roots, are they all unwholesome states?
Whatever states are rooted in the same root as the unwholesome roots, are they all mutually rooted in one another by way of the unwholesome roots?
Or, whatever states have mutual roots by way of an unwholesome root, are all those states unwholesome?
1.1.1.2.4. The Method of Root-Roots:
Whatever states are unwholesome, are they all rooted in an unwholesome root?
Furthermore, are all those phenomena which have an unwholesome root as their root themselves unwholesome?
And are all those phenomena which are unwholesome rooted in the same root as an unwholesome root?
Furthermore, are all those phenomena which have the same root as an unwholesome root themselves unwholesome?
Whatever phenomena have a single root-rooted basis with an unwholesome root, are they all mutually root-rooted with that unwholesome root?
Or conversely, whatever phenomena are mutually root-rooted with an unwholesome root, are all those phenomena unwholesome?
1.1.1.3. The Fourfold Guide-Line on the Indeterminate Category (*Abyākatapada-nayacatukka*)
1.1.1.3.1. Fundamental Method:
Are all those phenomena that are indeterminate (abyākata) rooted in the indeterminate?
Or conversely, are all those phenomena that are rooted in the indeterminate themselves indeterminate?
Are all those states which are indeterminate (abyākata) rooted in the same root as the indeterminate roots?
Or again, are all those states which are rooted in the same root as the indeterminate roots necessarily indeterminate?
Are all those states which are rooted in the same root as the indeterminate roots mutually rooted in one another with respect to the indeterminate roots?
Or, are all those phenomena which have mutual roots by way of an indeterminate root themselves indeterminate?
1.1.1.3.2. The Method of Root-Roots:
Are all those phenomena that are indeterminate rooted in an indeterminate root?
Or again, are all those things which have the indeterminate root as their root themselves indeterminate?
And are all those things which are indeterminate likewise rooted in the same single root as the indeterminate root?
Or again, are all those things which have the indeterminate root as their single root themselves indeterminate?
Whatever phenomena have a single root-root with an indeterminate root, are they all mutually root-roots with that indeterminate root?
Or conversely, whatever phenomena are mutually root-roots with an indeterminate root, are all those phenomena indeterminate?
1.1.1.3.3. The Root-Manner (Mūlakanaya).
Are all those states which are indeterminate rooted in the indeterminate?
Or conversely, are all those states which are rooted in the indeterminate themselves indeterminate?
Are all those states which are indeterminate rooted in the same root as that which is the indeterminate root?
Furthermore, are all those phenomena which have a single root with an indeterminate root themselves indeterminate?
Are all those phenomena which have a single root with an indeterminate root mutually rooted with that indeterminate root?
Furthermore, are all those phenomena which are mutually rooted with an indeterminate root themselves indeterminate?
1.1.1.3.4. The Root-and-Root Method (Mūlamūlakanaya):
Are all those states that are indeterminate (abyākata) rooted in an indeterminate root?
Or conversely, are all those states that are rooted in an indeterminate root themselves indeterminate?
Are all those states which are indeterminate rooted in the same root as the indeterminate roots?
Or conversely, are all those states which are rooted in the same root as the indeterminate roots necessarily indeterminate?
Are all those states which are rooted in the same root as the indeterminate roots mutually rooted in one another as roots with the indeterminate roots?
Or again, those states which, by way of an indeterminate root, are rooted in one another—Are all those states indeterminate?
1.1.1.4. The Fourfold Scheme of the Name-Section (Nāmapada Nayacatukka).
1.1.1.3.1. The Root-Scheme (Mūlanaya).
Are all those phenomena that are mental (nāma), all rooted in the mental?
Or conversely, are all those things rooted in the mental, all phenomena that are mental?
Are all those phenomena that are mental, all rooted in the same root as the mental?
Or again, are all those phenomena which share the same root as the root of mind (nāmamūla) themselves mind?
And are all those phenomena which share the same root as the root of mind mutually rooted in one another by virtue of that root of mind?
Or again, are all those phenomena which are mutually rooted in one another by virtue of the root of mind themselves mind?
1.1.1.3.2. The Root-of-Roots Method (Mūlamūlanaya):
Are all those things that are mental phenomena (nāma-dhammas) rooted in the root of the mental (nāmamūlamūla)?
Or conversely, are all those things that are rooted in the root of the mental mental phenomena?
Whatever phenomena there are that are mental, are they all rooted in the same root as the mental roots?
Or conversely, whatever phenomena are rooted in the same root as the mental roots, are they all mental phenomena?
Whatever phenomena are rooted in the same root as the mental roots, are they all mutually rooted with the mental roots?
Or again, are all those phenomena which have mutual roots by way of name-roots also name-phenomena?
1.1.1.3.3. The Method of Roots:
Are all whatever phenomena that are names also rooted in names?
Or again, are all those phenomena which have name as their root "mental"?
And are all those phenomena which are mental rooted in the same root as name?
Or again, are all those phenomena which are rooted in the same root as name "mental"?
Whatever phenomena have the name-root as their root, do they all have one another as their roots by way of the name-root?
Or, whatever phenomena have one another as their roots by way of the name-root, are they all name-phenomena?
1.1.1.3.4. The Method of the Root-of-Roots.
Are all those phenomena that are mental (nāma), all rooted in the root of the mental?
Or again, are all those phenomena that are rooted in the root of the mental, all mental?
Are all those phenomena that are mental, all rooted in the same root as the root of the mental?
Or, are all those phenomena which have the same root-root as the name-root themselves names?
Are all those phenomena which have the same root-root as the name-root mutually root-roots with respect to the name-root?
Or, are all those phenomena which are mutually root-roots with respect to the name-root themselves names?
The Exposition of the Root Chapter.
